title: Space Tech Briefing — September 29, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! This is your daily dose of the cosmos, live from Space Technology Radio, and I'm your host, ready to launch you into the latest and greatest. It is September 29, 2026, and what a start to the week it has been!

We begin with monumental news that has everyone buzzing: SpaceX's Starship has successfully reached orbit for the very first time! This incredible milestone was achieved just yesterday, Monday, September 28th, marking a pivotal moment in space exploration. The mission saw a Super Heavy Block 3, Booster 21, paired with Starship Ship 41, a V3 version, making its fourteenth flight. The primary goal was to place Starship into a low Earth orbit, approximately 275 kilometers high, for about six Earth revolutions, spanning roughly ten hours. And it delivered! The entire flight sequence was tested: flawless stage separation, a controlled return and splashdown of the Super Heavy booster in the Gulf of Mexico, followed by the Starship's deorbit, atmospheric re-entry, and a precise splashdown in the Pacific, just west of Chile. This flight was focused purely on proving the orbital capability, so no recovery with the launch tower was planned this time. What an incredible step forward for humanity's journey to the stars!

And as we celebrate yesterday's groundbreaking launch, let's also look back at a major recent development in deep space exploration. The European Space Agency's JUICE probe, on its epic voyage to Jupiter, recently made another close pass by our home planet. This crucial maneuver, a gravity assist, skillfully utilized Earth's gravitational pull to fine-tune JUICE's trajectory, ensuring its safe and precise arrival at Jupiter in 2031. During this flyby, all of JUICE's scientific instruments were activated, gathering valuable data as it sped past, confirming everything is in perfect working order for its ultimate mission to the gas giant and its icy moons. Steady progress for a mission set to unlock the secrets of our solar system's largest planet!

And that's your morning briefing from Space Technology Radio. Keep looking up, stay curious, and join us again tomorrow for more cosmic updates. Have a fantastic day!
